newsitem.title: UK: ICI confirms H1 profit plunge.
newsitem.headline: ICI confirms H1 profit plunge.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc on Thursday confirmed a sharp drop in first-half profits, blaming a strong pound and a continued collapse in bulk chemical prices.
ICI said pre-tax profit fell to 160 million pounds from 367 million a year before, with sales slipping 6.2 percent to 4.97 billion pounds.

The chief culprits were the titanium dioxide and polyester operations, both of which were sold to DuPont & Co last week in a $3 billion deal. ICI flagged its likely first-half result at the same time.

ICI said falls in commodity chemical prices, notably polyester and tioxide, and the impact of sterling's rise wiped 300 million pounds ($502.6 million) off profits in the first half. The pound accounted for some 90 million pounds of the drop.

ICI's sale of half its bulk chemical operations last week is helping to fund ICI's transformation into a speciality chemicals business, largely through the acquisition of Unilever Plc's speciality chemicals arm for $8 billion.
"Quarter two has been a defining period in the history of ICI which will secure its future well into the next century," ICI chairman Sir Ronald Hampel said in a statement. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
